item.title: Ben Nevis Holiday Park Celebrates Third Successive Tourism Award
item.description: Ben Nevis Holiday Park has been named Scotland’s Best Large Relax and Explore destination for the third year running, reflecting exceptional guest reviews and reinforcing the Highlands as one of the UK’s most reliable and welcoming staycation regions.The post Ben Nevis Holiday Park Celebrates Third Successive Tourism Award appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: New Head Brewer Appointed at Inverness Brewstillery
item.description: Uile bheist in Inverness has appointed experienced brewer Charlotte Cook as its new Head Brewer ahead of a major year for the city, bringing fresh creativity and ambition as the brewery prepares for rising visitor numbers and new opportunities.The post New Head Brewer Appointed at Inverness Brewstillery appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Highland Concerns as British Transport Police Trial Live Facial Recognition in London Stations
item.description: A new police trial of Live Facial Recognition technology in London rail stations is being watched closely in the Highlands, where privacy and freedom remain prized, as British Transport Police assesses whether the system improves safety or raises new concerns for travellers.The post Highland Concerns as British Transport Police Trial Live Facial Recognition in London Stations appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Delivering Educational Improvements Across Scotland’s Schools
item.description: New national statistics show record highs in literacy and numeracy, rising attendance and improving teacher numbers across Scotland’s schools, signalling a stronger recovery from the pandemic and a narrowing attainment gap that reflects the steady long term efforts of pupils, staff and communities.The post Delivering Educational Improvements Across Scotland’s Schools appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Transforming Equality and Human Rights Across Scotland’s Public Sector
item.description: Scotland has launched a new strategy, action plan and toolkit to help public bodies embed equality and human rights into everyday decisions. With more than one hundred resources now in one place, the move signals a clear national commitment to fairness and long-term cultural change.The post Transforming Equality and Human Rights Across Scotland’s Public Sector appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Jamie Stone Warns Digital ID Plan Risks Leaving Highland Communities Behind
item.description: Public concern over digital ID plans has surged across the Highlands, with Jamie Stone warning the policy risks deepening digital exclusion in rural communities. With thousands backing a petition, pressure is growing on the UK Government to rethink its approach.The post Jamie Stone Warns Digital ID Plan Risks Leaving Highland Communities Behind appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Starmer Urged to Scrap £108 Energy Bill Hike as Costs Rise Again for Scottish Families
item.description: Scottish households face another energy bill increase as Ofgem confirms higher network charges, prompting Stephen Flynn to demand Labour scrap the £108 hike. The SNP argues Scotland’s energy wealth should reduce bills, not drive them higher.The post Starmer Urged to Scrap £108 Energy Bill Hike as Costs Rise Again for Scottish Families appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Islands Business Resilience Fund Expanded to Support More Communities
item.description: The Islands Business Resilience Fund has been expanded to support more communities hit by ferry disruption, offering vital help for businesses across the west coast and Small Isles as the Scottish Government and HIE work to strengthen economic resilience.The post Islands Business Resilience Fund Expanded to Support More Communities appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: New Gaelic Initiative Aims to Drive Jobs and Economic Growth Across Highland Communities
item.description: A new national initiative, Tog, has been launched to link Gaelic directly to jobs and economic growth, focusing investment on the communities where the language is strongest and supporting businesses, entrepreneurs and young people across the Highlands and Islands.The post New Gaelic Initiative Aims to Drive Jobs and Economic Growth Across Highland Communities appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: First Minister Warns of Existential Threat to Key Scottish Industries Without Urgent UK Government Action
item.description: First Minister John Swinney has warned the UK Government to act now or risk irreversible deindustrialisation, urging the removal of the Energy Profits Levy and stronger support for Scotland’s energy and whisky sectors as key industries face mounting pressures and long term threats.The post First Minister Warns of Existential Threat to Key Scottish Industries Without Urgent UK Government Action appeared first on The Highland Times.
